records.material_pending_reason: The chosen southern opening, westward transfer and northward turn through the first pond connections are not established. The downstream valley, Watts–Françoys-Malherbe lake branch, lower Déception junction and marine outlet are separately supported.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected middle and lower route corresponds to the Watts–Françoys-Malherbe lake branch, its northern junction with the Déception river corridor, and the outlet into Baie Déception on Hudson Strait. Independent imagery supports the successive lake, inter-lake, junction and terminal settings. It does not establish a continuous through-link across the selected southern westward transfer, its northward turn and the first small-pond connections. A receiving river name and regional glacial-valley description cannot close that gap; the entire selected group remains in one material-pending state.
records.completion_scope: All 18 parts are addressed. Middle and lower geographic correspondence is supported, while the chosen opening and initial transfer remain incomplete; no completed representative system or naming-scope hold is claimed.
records.supported_name_scope: Rivière Déception identifies the receiving lower river after the Watts and Françoys-Malherbe lake branch joins the east-arriving river. The two lake names are distinct components, not aliases of the river, and the selected southern feeder remains unnamed and materially unresolved.

scope_limits: The selected southern opening and westward-to-northward through-transfer are not established as one continuous corridor.
No name is assigned to the initial feeder or every tributary; lower receiving-system identity does not authorize a scalar name for the selection.
Lake and major-join correspondence is regional/corridor scale; present water level, ice, flow direction and exact banks are not established.
The imagery scenes lack verified acquisition dates and do not establish current conditions.

records.region: Interior Chubut, Sacanana valley, Gan Gan plain and Laguna Verde terminal basin
records.geographic_disambiguation: Independent EDiPA prose identifies intermittent Arroyo Sacanana from the Pirrey Mahuida area past Gan Gan to Laguna Verde near Chacay Oeste. Three successfully inspected Esri imagery views establish the supplied opening feeder, its intervening joins, the middle and lower alluvial corridor and the actual endpoint inside the terminal lake/playa basin. Together they support a bounded representative Sacanana-system identity; they do not supply an official registry entry or one scalar name for every selected surface.
records.completion_scope: All 28 selected parts, unnamed opening feeder, valley joins, intermittent alluvial corridor and actual terminal inside Laguna Verde are supported at ordinary corridor scale by three imagery views combined with the independent regional course account.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity of the connected Sacanana drainage corridor, including an unnamed chosen northwestern feeder, the southward valley and eastward intermittent alluvial course past Gan Gan, and the actual final passage within Laguna Verde. The river name is not assigned to the unnamed opening feeder, every side channel, wetland-like patch or terminal lake floor.

scope_limits: Arroyo Sacanana is a representative system identity inferred from the combined regional name-and-course account and directly viewed physical corridor, not from labels printed on the imagery.
The chosen upper feeder has no separately established local name; the formal start of the Sacanana name is unassigned.

Current surface water, continuous seasonal flow, exact shoreline, small branch allocation and wetland classification are not established. Dry alluvial reaches are not treated as gaps solely because they are dry.
The terminal lake/playa floor has a distinct waterbody role and is not assigned the river name as a scalar.

The optional Chubut presentation was unavailable. Uninspected Hidroar/Navidad and CFI Sacanana material was not used as replacement evidence while its relationship to that presentation remained unresolved.

records.material_pending_reason: The chosen opening and westward inland course, both fragment joins, northward lower route and specific final estuarine channel lack permitted primary source correspondence.
records.geographic_disambiguation: The supplied selection begins inland east of the lower Iscuandé corridor, trends west through the upper reach, turns north through the coastal plain and ends at the Pacific coastal side of the Iscuandé delta. Broad delta membership does not establish the specific selected terminal channel or the headward branch.
records.completion_scope: All three mainstem fragments and stages are recorded. The Iscuandé delta name and regional coastal setting are supported, but selected opening, inland path, both joins, lower estuarine passage and actual terminal remain materially incomplete.
records.supported_name_scope: Coastal receiving-river and named delta candidate only. The chosen opening and the complete inland through-route are not yet established from permitted primary geographic evidence.

scope_limits: Río Iscuandé is a lower receiving/delta candidate, not a completed representative identity for all selected components.
El Turbio and Bracito remain unadopted discovery leads; neither is established as an alias of Iscuandé.
The full correspondence gap is about substantial through-links, not exact banks, vertices, discharge or current operations.
Formal registry identity, name-transition positions and Korean rendering remain unverified.

records.region: Southern Georgia and Florida Big Bend, Aucilla River corridor
records.geographic_disambiguation: The selected unnamed Georgia feeder connects to the Aucilla river, pond and swamp corridor, distinct Little Aucilla and Wacissa tributary joins, the explained lower karst sequence and the actual Gulf mouth. Four views of the same USGSTopo service support cartographic correspondence, supplemented by independent authorial prose.
records.completion_scope: Complete at ordinary regional/corridor scale for every supplied mainstem part, chosen opening, major joining setting, pond/lake/wetland and karst passages, and actual terminal. This is a representative system determination, not an automatic application.
records.supported_name_scope: Representative identity for the supplied northern feeder–Aucilla corridor through upper ponds, Aucilla Swamp, Sneads Smokehouse Lake, Little Aucilla junction, lower channel, sink/resurgence sequence and Gulf mouth. Distinct tributaries, lakes, ponds and karst features are not assigned a single scalar name.

scope_limits: The headward selected approach has no separately supported name and is not asserted to be the unique natural source of the river.
The river system contains wetlands, ponds, a distinctly named lake and repeated underground passages; this evidence does not imply uninterrupted open surface water or year-round navigability.
No exact pointwise name-transition, bank alignment, present water level, underground conduit geometry or canal-operation state is established.
Formal registry identity, standardized Korean name and whole-feature scalar naming remain unverified.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. Keep base records, scope clauses, region qualifiers and assessment histories unchanged. Apply explicit status-list changes. Subtract all recorded IDs from the exact eligible initial inventory to recover unrecorded targets; pending IDs remain recorded but are not completed source reviews.
publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
